claim: A Systematic Investment Plan (SIP) allows an investor to regularly invest a fixed amount of money, starting as low as Rs 500, in a mutual fund scheme at regular intervals like once a month or once a quarter
Each instalment buys mutual fund units at that day's price, known as the NAV
When prices are low, the fixed amount buys more units, and when prices are high, it buys fewer units, which is called rupee cost averaging
Inflation matters for long-term goals because a goal priced in today's rupees, such as a house or a child's education, will usually cost more when the money is actually needed
As prices rise over time, the purchasing power of money falls, meaning the same amount of money buys less
Therefore, planning with today's price alone can leave a goal underfunded, and the longer the time horizon, the bigger this difference will be
SEBI defines diversification as a process that reduces risk by investing in various financial instruments, industries, and other categories
It follows the common saying of not putting all your eggs in one basket
This helps lower overall portfolio swings because different investments do not all move in the same direction by the same amount at the same time
An emergency fund helps you handle unexpected events like job loss, illness, or urgent repairs without needing to sell your investments at a bad time or borrow money at high interest
Keeping this reserve protects your long-term investments from being broken early
Money for emergencies should be kept in safe, liquid places instead of in investments whose value can fall sharply

According to financial education booklets, gold acts as a diversification component in sample portfolios, usually making up 10% to 15% of the total mix alongside equity and debt rather than serving as the main holding
In illustrative tables, the app keeps gold at a 10% allocation
Prices of gold can fluctuate and it does not pay regular interest like debt
Equity funds can lose value due to market risk from economy-wide factors
unsystematic risk from problems in a specific company or industry
volatility risk causing sharp price swings in short periods
business risk when a company performs badly or fails
The value of an equity fund changes every day with the prices of the shares it holds
An expense ratio represents a scheme's annual operating expenses expressed as a percentage of its daily net assets
which goes toward running costs
an expense ratio of 1% a year means about 1% of the scheme's assets are used for these expenses
Higher expenses will reduce the return that an investor receives
